gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'No, I won't open the door,' he said. He ___ to open the door.
gaps.explanation: Refusals are reported with refuse + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'She arrived last night,' he told us. He told us that she had arrived ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' becomes the night before (the previous night) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' he said. He said he would see me ___.
gaps.explanation: Time expressions shift: tomorrow becomes the next day / the following day.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you finished the report?' the boss asked. The boss asked ___ finished the report.
gaps.hint: present perfect → past perfect in a yes/no question
gaps.explanation: Have you finished → whether/if I had finished; statement word order throughout.

gaps.sentence: They ___ breaking the window, but nobody believed them.
gaps.explanation: Deny + -ing reports a rejection of the accusation; 'but nobody believed them' confirms the meaning.

gaps.sentence: The colonel ___ his soldiers to advance at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Order + object + to-infinitive reports a command; suggest and hope do not take object + infinitive.
